It is the contention of the petitioner that demand notice that was made on 26-7-1984 demanding an amount of Taka 3,46,662.91 towards the excise duties and sales tax on 300 bales of finished Jute goods which were taken out of the Mills premises on 8-8-1979 for exporting was not legally recoverable since demand was made beyond 3 years from the date ie 8-8-1979 the excise duties and sales tax on the goods taken out of the mill premises to export became due but the boat that was carrying the goods capsized in the river and subsequently the goods was not exported. It is also the contention of the petitioner that claim of excise duties and sales tax on the basis of the amendment made in Rule 10 providing 5 years (prior to amendment it was 3 years) as the period for making demand of the recoverable duties and taxes under the Salt Excise Rule, 1944 was not legal since excise duties and sales tax, if any, were recoverable from the petitioner in respect of 300 bales of finished jute goods which were taken out from the mill premises for export purpose on 8-8-1979 became barred by limitation as because at the material time law as to making of demand for recoverable excise duties and sales taxes was 3 years and, as such, customs authority was required to make the demand within that period. Further contention of the petitioner is that the appellate authority and the revisional authority were in error in not considering the material fact with the demand that was made by the respondent No. 5 Deputy Collector, Customs and Excise, Khulna, Customs and Excise Division, Khulna was barred by time and, as such, demand so made was illegal. 

 6. Learned Deputy Attorney-General has submitted that since petitioner did not dispute its liability of paying the duties and sales tax in respect of the goods which it took out on 8-8-1979 to export and that as petitioner did not inform the respondent 4 about the fact that the barge that was carrying the goods taken out on 8-8-1979 capsized and that thereupon Insurance Company salvaged part of the goods ie 42.45 metric tons, and that sold the same in the local market and that rest of the goods could not be salvaged, as such, petitioner could not absolve itself of the liability to pay the duties and sales tax in respect of the goods taken out without payment of levies for export no illegality has been committed by the respondents in making the demand for outstanding excise duties and sales tax. He also submits that the petitioner having had not availed of the forum wherein he could have raised the question of limitation, as such, upon raising the contention of limitation he cannot maintain the present writ petition upon raising the complicated contention of limitation adjudication whereof needs investigation of contentious facts. 

 7. Undisputed position is that petitioner company took out 121.98 metric tons (in 300 bales) of finished jute goods on 8-8-1979 from the mills premises to export. It is also not disputed that the barge that was carrying the said goods capsized and that part of the goods salvaged was sold in the local market and the major portion of the goods remained untraceable. It is the petitioner's contention that as the goods could not be exported and that excise duties and sales tax livable on the goods as were not the part of the Insurance Policy that was taken out in respect of the goods mentioned hereinabove and, as such, excise duties and sales tax that was livable on the goods taken out for export but ultimately could not be exported it was not required to pay the duties and sales tax. The petitioner is also questioning the legality of the demand that was made by the respondent No. 5 by the demand notice dated 26-7-1984 on the ground of limitation or, in other words, it is the contention of the petitioner that the excise duties and sales tax even if were livable on the goods that was taken out from the mill premises on 8-8-1979 for exporting and was realisable but the demand having not been made within three years from the date of taking out the goods for export ie within three years from 8-8-1979 as was prescribed in Rule 10 of the Rule prior to amendment thereof and thereupon the claim of excise duties and sales tax having become barred, the respondents cannot make the claims on the basis of the amended provision of Rule 10 of the Rule whereby period for making demand/claim was extended to 5 years from 3 years. Excise duties and sales tax that was livable on the goods that was taken out from the mills premises on 8-8-1979 for export became dues on and from that date. Under unamended Rule 10 of the Rule respondent 3 was required to make demand of the excise duties and sales tax due in respect of the goods that was taken out on 8-8-1979 within 3 years from that date ie 8-8-1979. Undoubtedly, period of 3 years as was in Rule 3 prior to its amendment on 30-6-1983 expired on 7-8-1982. As seen from the Affidavit-in-Opposition that show cause notice to the petitioner mill was issued on 28-11-1983 and that petitioner replied to the show cause notice. Thereafter, the respondents issued the demand notice on 26-7-1984 for the outstanding excise duties and sales tax in respect of the goods that was taken out from the mill premises on 8-8-1979.
